title: NetRen: Service Migration-Driven Network Renascence with Synthesizing Updated Configuration
problem: Enterprise networks require efficient configuration updates when services and traffic patterns change. Manual configuration updates are slow, lead to poor performance, and have handling limitations that affect network availability.
motivation: Automated and efficient network reconfiguration is critical for maintaining network availability and performance during service migrations.
method: NetRen uses three stages to generate network configurations. First, sketch extraction converts the network into a graph showing all devices and connections. Second, a GraphTrans synthesizer combines this graph representation with Transformers—a machine learning technique that examines many relationships simultaneously to recognize patterns—to generate routing configurations (OSPF and BGP are protocols that direct how network traffic flows) by learning from examples showing how different configurations perform. Third, a stepwise repairer fixes violations to ensure the configuration works.
key_novelty: The core innovation is the GraphTrans synthesizer, which learns to generate routing instructions by combining graph representations with Transformers (machine learning that learns patterns) and training on examples that show how network performance relates to different configurations.
contributions: GraphTrans synthesizer for synthesizing OSPF/BGP configurations from graph sketches using Transformers with parallel reasoning
Configuration repair mechanism using well-initialized solutions to overcome satisfiability constraints
312.4× improvement in synthesis efficiency compared to baseline approaches
5.83% network performance improvement with 98% output configuration consistency
